data.description: International Code of Zoological Nomenclature. Accepts only Latin characters.
International Code of Botanical Nomenclature. Accepts Proper Case Latin strings for higher taxonomy; Latin characters, the multiplication sign, and dash for Genus through "subspecies."
Default value for names which have not been properly filed yet. This should never be used for the creation of new names.
Names which are explicitly disallowed by the various Codes, but which have current or historical value. Examples include botanical names containing umlauts.

International Code of Phylogenetic Nomenclature, or PhyloCode, a set of rules governing phylogenetic nomenclature to regulate the naming of clades, governance of species names is left to rank-based Nomenclature codes (ICN, ICZN, ICBN, ICTV).
International Code of Nomenclature of Prokaryotes. Formerly the International Code of Nomenclature of Bacteria (ICNB) or Bacteriological Code (BC).
International Committee on Taxonomy of Viruses
